title: Signage development examples
slide_intent: Teach designers to compare a saturated field with its reversed version in the actual architectural setting.
strategic_value: Millennium Gallery can retain its pink identity while choosing how strongly a building-scale panel competes with its surroundings.
demonstration: Matching photographs show the same façade sign with white lettering on pink and pink lettering on white. The mark, list of activities and seal keep the same order.
practical_value: Evaluate both polarity options against the façade before choosing the sign ground.

content_islands.name: Pink-ground study
content_islands.spec: Show the venue mark above the stacked Art, Craft, Design, Shop and Cafe message. Place the small seal below, all in white.

content_islands.name: White-ground study
content_islands.spec: Repeat the same site view, size and arrangement with pink type on white. Align the photographs so the change of ground is easy to compare.

reference_purposes.Expression: The two façade studies compare a dominant pink field with pink lettering on white.
reference_purposes.Application: Matched building views show the color reversal at architectural scale.

ingredient.name: Millennium Gallery signage pink
ingredient.role: Identify the gallery while changing how much of the façade carries its color.
ingredient.application: Compare white lettering on pink with pink lettering on white while holding the site, sign dimensions and hierarchy steady.
ingredient.scope: These are two indicative signage-development examples. The page does not choose a preferred option or prescribe one treatment for all gallery signs.
